Book correction: No function can satisfy f(x) + f(-x) = x^2 + x^3 for all x: replacing x by -x leaves the left side unchanged but turns the right side into x^2 - x^3, so we would need x^3 = 0 for every x. (At x = 1 the condition says f(1) + f(-1) = 2, at x = -1 it says f(-1) + f(1) = 0.) Because the left side is always even, only the even part x^2 can be meant: f(x) + f(-x) = x^2 (for example f(x) = \frac{x^2}{2}
